name: Photo picker
plain: A system gallery picker that returns only chosen photos with no permission.
meaning: Reveals only the items the person selects. Recommended by both platforms.

android.store_policy: Play: preferred over READ_MEDIA_* for most apps
android.note: Backported to older versions through Google Play services.

limits.headline: Can open only the photos you pick from a system gallery, with no permission asked
limits.user_action: You tap Choose photo or Attach image and select photos in the system picker
can: Open the one or more photos you pick
Upload or edit the chosen photos
Work with no permission prompt at all
Work on older Android versions through Google Play services
cannot: See any photo you did not tap
Browse your gallery itself; the system does that in its own window
Keep access after the pick, except to the files you chose

story.what_it_is: A system window that hands an app only the photos you choose.

marketing.name: Android photo picker
marketing.pitch: Developer pitch: a safe, simple way for users to pick photos and videos with no permission needed.

marketing.name: PHPicker
marketing.pitch: Developer pitch: a system picker that lets people choose photos without giving an app access to the whole library.

story.for_you: You tap Add photo and the system gallery opens. You pick a few pictures and the app gets only those. No scary permission pop up shows, and the app cannot see anything else.
story.for_makers: Makers skip the permission step and the store review burden. They still get what they need for posts and uploads. Both platforms now push apps toward this picker.

use_cases.example: You post three pictures to a feed and the app sees only those three.
A chat app sends a photo with no gallery permission.
A reviews page lets you add a product photo.
A game lets you set a profile avatar from one photo.
A bank app takes one picture of a check from your gallery.
A dating app lets you add profile pictures one at a time.
A collage app lets you pick a few photos to start a project.

risks: App still sees what you pick
story.android_note: The system photo picker needs no permission, and works back through Google Play services.
story.ios_note: PHPicker needs no permission and runs outside the app.

technical_bounds: Metadata like GPS may still be inside the file

history.change: Photo picker with Play services backport to Android 4.4
